Negative numbers

Care worker

Care services

\(\displaystyle \text{balance} = \text{in} - \text{out}\)

Is this patient taking in enough fluid?

Uses example figures: the numbers marked (example figure) or (example figures) are made up to show the method.

A fluid chart records what goes in (drinks) and what comes out. The balance is in − out; a negative balance means more out than in. Drinks: 250, 200, 300, 150, 250, 200 ml. Out: 1500 ml (example figures).

  1. In: \(250 + 200 + 300 + 150 + 250 + 200 = 1350\) ml.
  2. Balance: \(1350 - 1500 = -150\) ml: more out than in, so tell the nurse.

The answer: \(1350 - 1500 = -150\) ml

Sources

Every job and every figure that is not an example comes from a public page you can check.
